premise_checks.premise: There exists a Yale financial relational-network paper that learns over dynamic relation graphs among financial entities and tests whether relations carry extra information by shuffling graph links or deleting network structure as controls.
searches_performed: OpenAlex works filter institutions.ror:03v76x132 (Yale University) AND title/abstract contains 'graph neural' - 100 hits, top 25 reviewed by title: brain/fMRI GNNs, traffic GNNs, IceCube, materials, robotics, hydrology-derived code - none is a financial relational-graph learning paper.

OpenAlex works filter institutions.ror:03v76x132 AND 'financial' AND 'graph' - 11 hits: Mamba/stock (authors UBC/SFU/Pittsburgh + Yale economist as last author), two AI-in-financial-regulation papers (Clayton/Coppola), smart-contract security, telemedicine-in-ICU, haematology - no match.
OpenAlex works filter institutions.ror:03v76x132 AND 'temporal graph' - 10 hits, all traffic/fMRI/music/water/wildlife; no finance.
OpenAlex fulltext search 'shuffled graph' + title/abstract 'financial' - 1 hit, a 2026 climate-risk/supply-chain paper, not Yale and not a link-shuffling control.
OpenAlex works filter title/abstract 'relational graph' AND 'stock' - 22 hits reviewed: all stock-relation GNN papers from CS groups (e.g. ICAIF 2024, DyRelNet 2026, IJCAI 2020), none from Yale.
Web search (3 query batches) for 'shuffle the edges' / 'degree-preserving rewiring' / 'placebo edges' in financial graph learning - no Yale paper surfaced.
premise_checks.finding: No single paper matching the description could be found. Three separate real works get conflated by the description.

closest_matches.why: This is the actual Yale-affiliated financial-ML paper (Bryan Kelly, Yale SOM, per the Crossref affiliation field). It is a machine-learning asset-pricing study over firm characteristics - not a relational graph, and it contains no edge-shuffling or structure-deletion control.

The closest methodological match to 'test whether relations carry information': it argues that a financial relation graph must be validated independently of the downstream model. But it is University College Dublin, not Yale, and its device is a set of graph-level interpretation tasks, not edge shuffling.

An example of a financial graph model that compares graph-derived shared information against individual information. Not Yale, no shuffled-link null, and the 'graph' is a stock-concept membership matrix.

premise_checks.conclusion: The premise should not be accepted as stated: I could not verify the existence of a Yale paper with this design. The specific methodological device (rewiring links while preserving degree/activity/time as a null) is standard network-science practice (configuration-model-style randomisation), not a Yale finance contribution. S-028 should cite it as a null-model design choice and cite R42/R43 for what they actually do, rather than attributing the design to a Yale precedent.

gaps_not_verified: Venue for R01 (TGAT), R02 (TGN), R04 (DySAT), R06 (DyRep), R10 (GraphMixer), R12 (R-GCN), R17, R18, R35, R44: the arXiv records carry no venue/journal_ref field and dblp/OpenReview were blocked, so the commonly cited venues (ICLR 2020, ICML 2020 workshop, WSDM 2020, ICLR 2019, ICLR 2023, ESWC 2018, ICLR 2024) are deliberately NOT asserted.
Year of publication for R20 (Rogers, Diffusion of Innovations, 5th ed.): the publisher page confirmed title, author, edition and ISBN, but 2003 is not visible in the fetched excerpt.

No abstract could be obtained for 21 of the 44 references (Crossref records carry no abstract for JSTOR/ACM/OUP/Wiley deposits). Those references are used at title/metadata level only, and are marked claim_scope='title_record'; the remaining 23 are marked claim_scope='abstract' and their substantive claims are quoted or closely paraphrased from the fetched abstract.
Volume/issue/pages for R36 (Bailey et al., JCF) were absent from the Crossref record and are omitted rather than guessed.
A journal version of R35 (Kapoor & Narayanan) is known to exist in Patterns 2023 but was not fetched, so only the arXiv v1 record is cited.

No systematic database search (Web of Science/Scopus/Google Scholar) was possible: Scholar is not fetchable and the other two need subscriptions. Coverage is therefore targeted, not exhaustive, and a publication bias toward well-known work is likely.
